text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank MOE for the SkillsFuture Level-Up scheme and enquire about the Mid-Career Training Allowance, specifically, what arrangements or provisions will be made regarding training allowance for Singaporeans who have been unemployed for more than a year.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: There are significant numbers of Singaporeans who lost their jobs during the COVID-19 years of 2019 to 2022.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They have been struggling to make ends meet through ad hoc or freelance contracts sporadically over the past three years.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Their annual income is a far cry from their last-employed full-time income.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: On the SkillsFuture Top-Up with targeted scope, I have spoken regularly on this over the past few years, and I am glad to see that the top-up is confined to selected training programmes, which are industry-oriented, with better employability outcomes.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How will SSG work with the industry to identify courses which are industry-oriented with better employability outcomes?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are often multiple training vendors for one type of training.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And instead of tying it for better employment outcomes, can we also have some of it tied to the productivity or improvement outcome it brings to the company?

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Chairman, in my Budget speech, I highlighted the issue faced by persons with disabilities (PwDs) when encountering training providers who are either unwilling or not equipped to provide necessary accommodations.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: This often results in PwDs being turned away or not receiving the support required to fully engage in further education and training opportunities.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: These accommodations could range from providing screen reader-friendly course materials and websites for those with visual impairments, to adjusting assessment methods to cater to an individual's disabilities.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Unfortunately, as the provision of reasonable accommodation is not yet a legal requirement in Singapore, PwDs have limited avenues for recourse in such situations.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: As Singapore continues to equip its workforce with the skills needed for an evolving economy, it is crucial that PwDs have equal access to skills upgrading opportunities to remain competitive.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: This is to ensure that PwDs are not left behind in the upskilling process and that they have the necessary support to thrive in a competitive job market.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am also concerned about those who are outside these groups, such as the non-ITE graduates and non-mid-career Singaporeans who are in low-skilled jobs, including some gig jobs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: How will MOE urge them to take up training and opportunities in emerging sectors, like the digital, care and green economies?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many Singaporeans aspire for further education beyond diplomas, including Master's degrees, for example, in fields like sustainability.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They want to take a second bite of the cherry of tertiary level studies.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Given these high costs though, how will MOE support these ambitions?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In addition, I seek MOE's inputs on whether the investment in certifiable diplomas means a move away from MOE's vision of a more eclectic mix of pathways to lifelong learning.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What about promoting more bite-sized, modular and skills-based certificates of competency, instead of going only for diplomas and, possibly later, degrees and other ambitions?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, I would like to continue to speak up for the lifelong learning needs of PwDs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The SkillsFuture course landscape offers a vibrant array of over 20,000 courses for adult learners, now further enriched by the SkillsFuture Level-Up initiatives and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: However, this vibrant and optimistic lifelong learning scenario does not extend to school graduates and adults with special educational needs (SEN).

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is regardless of whether they graduate from SPED schools or mainstream schools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: To ignore the "cliff effect" of learners with disabilities or SEN would be to create a larger pool of Singaporeans relying on state welfare and who might be leading sub-optimal lives at adulthood.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, Sir, while MOE, SG Enable and their learning partners have made commendable efforts to support recent school graduates, these initiatives are insufficient to ensure lifelong learning for all.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Current learning efforts often appear fragmented and constrained by the scope and budgets of each Ministry, making it challenging to discern a unified vision or ecosystem where these efforts synergise.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This would pave the way for a more robust vision and the development of a more strategic, cohesive Lifelong Learning Plan for All.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Innovative, cost-effective learning solutions should be explored, for instance, rather than merely reducing fees for SPED schools, which are, of course, welcomed, could we also direct or add some grants to support learning into adulthood in MOE schools and beyond?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In summary, I urge MOE to refine its strategy for lifelong learning to include all Singaporeans, ensuring no one is left behind.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I urge MOE to take its place and lead in developing a more inclusive and comprehensive learning ecosystem for all Singaporeans, regardless of ability and background.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: What flexibility is allowed for students to discover courses other than the ones they initially took?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I have known of students who change their interest halfway through and they would like to try something else.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: What support systems, both academic and focused on mental well-being, would we provide prospective diploma students, especially those who have not been engaged in formal study for a long time?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: This support would alleviate the financial and emotional burden on students and their families, making it easier for graduates to commit to further education.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I have known such collaborations would actually encourage not just the students but the IHLs to work closely with the companies and hence, it is a win-win situation for all parties.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: By doing so, we ensure that the skills, knowledge and mental resilience acquired by the graduates are relevant and highly sought after by employers, and this enhances their employability and, of course, their career progression opportunities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, over the years, ITE has evolved significantly to meet the changing needs of Singapore's economy and workforce.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Initially focused on providing basic vocational skills training, ITE has expanded its curriculum to offer a wide range of courses catering to various industries, such as engineering, design, business, hospitality and healthcare.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This evolution reflects Singapore's shift towards a knowledge-based economy and the growing demand for skilled workers in the diverse sectors.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One key aspect of ITE's evolution is its emphasis on providing students with not just technical skills, but also soft skills and employability skills.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: ITE, indeed, places a strong emphasis on holistic education, ensuring that graduates are equipped with communication skills, problem-solving abilities, teamwork capabilities and a strong work ethic.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: During my time in polytechnic, I had a chance to work with many such ITE graduates who went on to polytechnic, and I can certainly testify to the quality of these students.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While ITE provides guidance and support to help graduates navigate future pathways and also informed decisions about their career aspirations, it is heartening to hear the Deputy Prime Minister mention the ITE Progress Award in his Budget speech.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also noted that Minister Chan Chun Sing had also talked about the ITE Progress Award in his Committee of Supply (COS) speech as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For many of them, they aspire towards graduation with a Higher Nitec certificate and then pursuing a diploma from the polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, not all of them will be able to get into a polytechnic and, for some, they may not be able to be admitted into a course of their interest in polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For some students, they are asked to consider a course in engineering when they are already struggling with Mathematics.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, it is a mismatch of the student's interest.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As a result, their only option is to go for the ITE Work-Study diploma.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Some of our ITE students are late bloomers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Is the WSDip widely accepted by employers within their specific industry?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How many companies are participating in the work-study programme?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: How are these employers equipped to deal with ITE students who are first-timers in the workforce and still have to take classes and study for their diploma at the same time?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Can the polytechnics consider expanding their classes to specially curate courses for ITE graduates which are more technical-based, rather than academic-based?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Here, I am talking about having separate polytechnic classes, vis-à-vis the usual polytechnic diplomas that are issued.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, there should be one specifically for ITE students.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: We should give the students every opportunity to pursue their dreams and the opportunity to graduate with a recognised polytechnic diploma.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Chairman, there is abundant research to show that the early years are critical to a child's development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am glad, therefore, that the Government had embarked on MOE Kindergartens and created an opportunity to develop a body of knowledge on the best pedagogies and practices for early childhood education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: As early childhood education has a significant impact on a child's trajectory, it becomes necessary to intervene early, especially if a child from a family in challenging circumstances is not given the full experience of quality education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Children from low-income families should not be denied an opportunity of education and programmes that could make a difference to their development and future success in life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Early childhood education and development are a key aspect of the strategy in sustaining social mobility.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The MOE Kindergarten is, therefore, also an important avenue to provide support for families in the lower-income group.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am, therefore, interested to learn about the plans that MOE Kindergarten has in the future to provide more services or support for low-income families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is heartening to note that there are meaningful services like Kindergarten Care (KCare) where parents who need full-day services can enrol their children in.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Would there be plans to enhance the support given to the families in need through further subsidies or programmes?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Evidence also suggests that students of engaged parents are more likely to do better, exhibit better social skills and adapt well to school.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Studies found a positive correlation between family involvement and student success, regardless of the family's socioeconomic status.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I commend MOE and neighbourhood schools for fostering Parent Support Groups (PSGs).

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: An overview of their achievements reveals that PSGs in Singapore have shown remarkable progress, enhancing the educational environment through various initiatives.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: My study of the landscape also shows that the level of PSG participation and contribution varies across schools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Additionally, I notice that many parents are still seized with worries over the high-stakes examinations, such as PSLE and GCEs, and direct school admissions as to what they perceived as better schools and also pressing issues, such as their children's mental health.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Parents, I believe, can be play a more significant and impactful role.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: MOE has the opportunity to devise a strategic plan for deeper collaboration with parents, fostering a culture that values learning beyond grades, growth beyond grades, supports good mental health and emphasises character development, all important mantras recited by the Minister for Education himself.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: MOE can draw inspiration from the organisational structures of multi-level networks in the business sector and also the cell group frameworks and resource support found in faith-based communities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: The nurturing environment that parents and PSGs create is foundational to our children's success, both academically and in their personal growth.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: With mental well-being emerging as a paramount concern in today's fast-paced and often stressful world, the collaboration between schools and parents has never been more critical.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Building on this and recognising the potential for even greater impact, I propose two further suggestions for consideration.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: This could serve as a comprehensive resource for parents by PSGs, facilitating easier access to information and best practices supporting mental well-being.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Such initiatives could provide a deeper understanding of how to recognise early signs of mental distress, foster open communication, create supportive environments and, finally, promote resilience in children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, our vision for an inclusive tomorrow starts with empowering our children to fulfil their potential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to meet the unique needs of our diverse learners and provide multiple pathways to support their aspirations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By bringing out the best in every student, we support the collective success of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through the Forward Singapore exercise, we have voiced our common desire for an inclusive Singapore that provides opportunities and empowers those in need.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MOE will continue improving access to quality education.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we want our children from the most vulnerable segment to have a strong start in their education journey.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Studies show that attending quality preschool can boost confidence and social skills and lay a strong foundation for life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In our local context, we have also found that children who attend preschool from age three are less likely to require learning support in Primary 1.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We know that lower-income families face multifaceted challenges requiring whole-of-community support, especially in ensuring early access to preschool.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: My colleagues from the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) will share about the wider preschool sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, all 55 MKs offer KCare for parents who require full-day care services for their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To improve the accessibility of MKs, we raised the household income cap for priority admission from $3,500 to $4,500 last year, reaching out to more children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But preschool fees may still deter some lower-income families from enrolling their children in preschool.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our Singapore Citizen children with working mothers are eligible for the KCare Additional Subsidy (AS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that this will further encourage preschool enrolment among our lower-income families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond that, we know that good attendance is also key.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thus, MOE is strengthening initiatives to facilitate regular attendance and provide learning support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will help narrow the gap in learning and development outcomes of children from lower-income families vis-à-vis their peers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These moves, alongside plans that my MSF colleagues will share, will give our children a strong start to their education journeys.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will continue supporting students who face difficulties in school due to challenges in their home settings through the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT), which was established in 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: UPLIFT provides holistic support through partnerships between schools and the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The UPLIFT Enhanced School Resourcing, another programme under UPLIFT, equips schools to provide customised help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, student care centres in all primary schools engage students meaningfully after school, while the GEAR-UP programme offers students in around 120 secondary schools mentoring and interest-based activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These programmes boost students’ socio-emotional competencies and their sense of belonging to school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The community also plays a key role in UPLIFT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2020, we piloted the UPLIFT Community Network (UCN) to coordinate support at the town level and to connect families with resources in the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More than six in 10 students improved in attendance, and seven in 10 parents showed improved parenting habits and parent-child relationships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Encouraged by this success, we expanded the network to more than 100 schools across all 24 towns nationwide in 2023.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, I spoke about strengthening whole-of-Government social service delivery alongside other agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To facilitate coordinated support, we have since started to integrate the UCN into the ComLink+, led by MSF.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our schools will continue to work closely with partners under ComLink+ to meet the students’ educational needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Third, we want to continue enabling students with special education needs (SEN) to fulfil their potential, by supporting them in appropriate educational settings that bring out their best.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about our SEN students in our MOE mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This includes the TRANsition Support for InTegration (TRANSIT) for Primary 1 students with social and behavioural needs, which has been implemented in 139 schools, with the remaining 43 coming onboard by 2026.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: All primary schools also have at least two SEN officers, who are trained to provide learning and behavioural support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Additionally, MOE connects with partners like SPARK, Unlocking ADHD and Dyslexia Association of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We value their role in also supporting students with SEN and their families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Faisal Manap and Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked how we can help students with moderate to severe SEN, who face higher costs due to the customised and specialised care required.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Government has worked closely with the community to increase funding for special education (SPED) schools over the years and spends more on education per child in a SPED school compared to a mainstream school.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The income eligibility criterion for the SPED Financial Assistance Scheme was also increased last January.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: More than 3,500 students and their families will benefit.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I would add that about 50% of all SPED students currently pay similar fees as students in the mainstream schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Together with efforts by MSF, I assure Members that SPED students and their families will be supported in their educational and caregiving needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To enhance the attractiveness of the SPED teaching profession, we have reviewed SPED teachers’ and teacher aides’ (TAs') salary guidelines to be commensurate with their expected roles, their responsibilities and their competencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Salaries for SPED TAs can increase by up to 15% from 2024.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: From this year, we will also increase starting salaries for SPED classroom teachers by up to 15% and by up to 17% for TAs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These salary enhancements will vary depending on individuals’ prevailing salaries, and their experience, competencies, job role and work performance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Funding will be provided to SSAs to implement them progressively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To strengthen SPED teachers’ capabilities, we will introduce more professional development programmes to develop expertise in supporting different disability profiles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A School Staff Developer will also be appointed in each SPED school to enable professional growth in all SPED teachers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We appreciate our SPED teachers and remain committed to supporting them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We agree with Mr Darryl David and Ms Denise Phua that preparing SPED students for post-school to community transition is very important.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: From age 13, SPED students are supported with transition planning, which facilitates progression to suitable post-school pathways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue taking a whole-of-Government approach to this, with MSF taking the lead.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond the Government’s efforts, students with SEN and their families need the community’s understanding and respect.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I assure Mr Ong Hua Han that students from mainstream and SPED schools are given opportunities to develop appreciation of differently abled peers, through meaningful and sustained interactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such efforts will help students with SEN integrate into the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Parents have shared with me their difficulties in navigating their everyday life with their SEN children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Those with autism, for instance, who struggle to regulate emotions, may exhibit anti-social behaviours like screaming.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Complaints from neighbours can lead to stressful visits from the relevant authorities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We do hope that the community is more supportive and understanding of their neighbours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our vision is for an inclusive Singapore, where families with SEN children feel at ease in their community, supported by understanding friends and neighbours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, I urge all Singaporeans to partner us in realising this vision.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, beyond supporting those in need, we will develop diverse pathways to support students’ aspirations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With the implementation of Full Subject-based Banding (Full SBB) in all secondary schools this year, students will take more subjects at different levels, based on learning needs and abilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have done away with the previous streaming categories and expanded post-secondary pathways to recognise diverse learner profiles and offer greater flexibility.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Members may also access this through the MP@SGPARL App.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Under the Full SBB, students can take subjects at G1, G2 or G3 subject levels, broadly mapped from the Normal (Technical), Normal (Academic) and the Express standards respectively.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Say, for example, in Secondary 3, Jude opts to pursue his passion in Design and Technology (D&T) as an elective, bringing him to six G3 subjects.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: After one year, he finds his curriculum load too challenging and he may decide to take D&T at a less demanding level at G2, which will enable him to pursue his passion still.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the end of Secondary 4, Jude will sit for five G3 and one G2 subject at the national examinations, the G2 being the D&T subject.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Today, for entry to polytechnic Year 1, Jude will not be able to use the G2 D&T grade as the current criteria is based on five G3 subjects, namely English Language; two Relevant (R) subjects, relevant to the course that he is applying for; and two Best (B) subjects.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: That is where the acronym ELR2B2 comes from.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Jude can thus use his G2 D&T grade if it improves his overall score.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: All students will be assessed on a common benchmark of four G3 subjects and one G2 subject.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Students with more G3 subjects will have their grades converted to G2, to determine the best G2 subject for admission.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I want to assure the House that this is not a tightening of the admissions criteria but a result of converting one B subject from G3 to G2.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For example, if Jude had an ELR2B2 of 26 points today, with a C6 in one of his B subjects, his C6 grade would be mapped to a G2 Grade 2.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This gives him an aggregate of 22 points, which will allow him to access polytechnic.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: If Jude chooses to take the B subject at G2 and obtains Grade 1, his aggregate score will improve to 21 points.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This change will allow our students to focus on their strengths, enjoy their learning more and take subjects at appropriate levels, aligned to their interests and needs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I will allow Members to digest what I have just said.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Chairman, let me highlight how we will uplift and support the continued learning of our ITE graduates.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We all are very passionate about the ITE students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We want them to do well and we want them to do well, not just in their studies but also in life.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They have built strong foundations in ITE but face a growing gap in their starting salaries compared to that of graduates from polytechnics and autonomous universities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: To provide more upskilling options for ITE graduates, ITE has expanded its Technical Diploma (TD) and the Work-Study Diploma (WSDip) offerings.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about employers' acceptance of WSDips.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Last year, close to 400 companies partnered ITE to offer WSDips, which were taken up by 1,150 ITE graduates.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These companies provide on-the-job training that complements the practice-based curriculum offered on campus.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The WSDip model is well-received as it allows both fresh and working ITE graduates to be employed full-time and receiving their ITE qualification salaries, because they go in with their ITE qualification already, while gaining up-to-date skills that can be immediately applied at work.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The continued ramp-up of ITE's diploma programmes will allow ITE graduates to choose the pathway aligned to their aspirations and needs, in addition to diplomas offered by polytechnics and arts institutions.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Employers, likewise, will be able to select diploma graduates who best fit their job profile and compensate them based on skills and experience.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Many ITE graduates I met want to deepen their skills.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I am sure many of our colleagues in the House have met them, as Mr Lim Biow Chuan has mentioned, at the Edusave ceremonies.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But they find it difficult to juggle studies and work and upskill only later in their careers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Hairul, for example, deferred his upskilling aspirations after graduating in 2017, to support his family.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Understandably, many of them do have family obligations and they want to support their families.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For Hairul's case, with his company's sponsorship, he recently completed the WSDip in Electrical Engineering as a top graduate and obtained a promotion and a pay raise to $2,500, commensurate to his diploma qualification and skillset.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will help ITE graduates like Hairul access a better wage trajectory by upskilling early.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: On diploma completion, they will receive a further $10,000 top-up to their CPF Ordinary Account (OA).

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These top-ups will help offset the costs of obtaining a diploma and boost their savings to support their longer-term goals.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I am pleased to inform Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Darryl David and Mr Sharael Taha that the IPA will be awarded from 2024 to eligible ITE graduates enrolling in diplomas issued by the polytechnics, ITE, Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and LASALLE College of the Arts, which meet industry needs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Singaporean ITE graduates who are currently enrolled in diplomas will also receive the OA top-up on diploma completion.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The IPA is our investment in the longer-term prospects of our ITE graduates.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With the IPA, more ITE graduates will deepen skills mastery and secure stronger progression prospects in their chosen careers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Chairman, our students should also play a role in creating a better future for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: One important area where our youth can make an impact is in sustainability.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is in line with MOE's support of the Singapore Green Plan 2030 and our goal to nurture stewards of the environment.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They will also drive change within their own households and communities to live a sustainable lifestyle.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Students will work with relevant agencies to monitor key indicators of change in the households they engage.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: In schools, students will continue to learn about sustainability issues under MOE's Eco Stewardship Programme.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Since our focus on food sustainability last year, more than 80% of our schools have enacted related initiatives on food security.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With these efforts, our students will be empowered as changemakers to make Singapore a sustainable home.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Pritam Singh has asked about the instruction of Non-Tamil Indian Languages (NTILs).

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: NTILs are taught through In-School Parallel Programmes (ISPPs) and Weekend Centres (WECs).

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Each request for new ISPPs is considered based on available resources and individual school needs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: When not feasible, the WEC provides a more viable option.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We also manage students' curriculum loads by ensuring that they do not take NTIL lessons in both ISPPs and WECs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As NTIL teachers are employed by Community Groups (CGs), MOE does not set guidelines on their salaries.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: MOE last reviewed the funding for NTIL learning in 2022 and will continue supporting the CGs in providing quality instruction.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay. :   To achieve our vision of an inclusive Singapore, where we accept and value contributions from every Singaporean.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Therefore, we must continue our efforts to fulfil the needs of diverse learners and develop multiple pathways that bring out the best in each child.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will continue to enhance efforts so that children from lower-income families, students with complex needs and students with special education needs are given better educational opportunities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will also work with social service agencies to raise salaries for SPED teachers and teacher aides, and strengthen their professional development.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With these, more students will be able to learn and grow, regardless of their background or needs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With most families using English dominantly in our homes, we recognise the importance of continuing efforts to deepen students’ interest in their mother tongue.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the primary level, starting this year, we are introducing a refreshed Malay language curriculum that uses more games and technology in the learning of Mother Tongue.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the secondary level, the Malay Language Learning and Promotion Committee will introduce a new competition for secondary school students this year.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This initiative builds on the success of the “Cepat Tepat” Quiz at the primary level, which is already in place.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This new competition aims to encourage the use of the Malay language beyond the classroom and promote interest in Malay culture and literature.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will continue to make Malay language learning more engaging, both in and out of school.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: At the polytechnics and ITE, we will introduce further shifts to support our students’ aspirations.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These changes will allow students to choose the subjects most suited to their own strengths and learning preferences.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We introduced the new ITE Progression Award (IPA) which aims to support our young ITE graduates to upskill to a diploma and secure more progression prospects.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The award helps with the costs of obtaining a diploma and reduces expenditure for their longer-term goals.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I urge more ITE graduates to press on with their upgrading efforts, so that they can deepen their skills and thrive in their chosen professions.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Apart from diploma courses in the polytechnics, they can also upskill through the ITE Work-Study programme or the Technical Diploma as well as LASALLE College of the Arts and NAFA diploma courses.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will continue our efforts to provide more learning pathways that can uplift our students’ capabilities to secure a better future for them. : Mr Chairman, it is our enduring mission to enable all to learn, progress and contribute.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With our community's help, we will support our students in charting their paths to meaningful vocations and diverse callings, to fulfil our shared goal of an inclusive success.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, lifelong learning is now a key pillar of our social compact.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Since the start of the SkillsFuture movement in 2015, we have built a strong lifelong learning ecosystem, comprising individuals, employers and training providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have expanded our partnerships to include NTUC, trade associations and chambers, professional bodies and SkillsFuture Queen Bee companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will continue to build on the foundation and expand our partnerships so that upskilling leads to better outcomes for both Singaporeans and businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: That is one in five in our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This includes both individual-initiated training where SkillsFuture Credit was used, as well as company-initiated training programmes, both of which were supported by SSG with subsidised course fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are introducing the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to further strengthen training support for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Members have asked how we can ensure good take-up and outcomes from this Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To do that, we must cater to the diversity of individuals' needs and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These courses are conducted by our IHLs and established private training providers, such as the NTUC Learning Hub and the Singapore Hotel Association Training and Education Centre (SHATEC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG will review the courses eligible for SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme over time, with input from sector agencies, industry intermediaries and professional bodies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Last Friday, Minister Chan Chun Sing spoke about the SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme (SCTP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SCTP courses are geared towards individuals who wish to move into high growth areas, such as the digital, care and green economies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: On top of training, SCTP courses include career advisory and employment facilitation, so that trainees have a better chance of getting employed after completing the course.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Take the example of Ms Low Danli, aged 41.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: She had been working in the ICT industry for 14 years when she sought a career change.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Low previously used her SkillsFuture Credit for some courses on corporate environment sustainability.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: After attending a SkillsFuture Roadshow, she took up an SCTP course in Sustainability at the SMU Academy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: With 90% Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy, the course fee payable by Ms Low was about $2,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: She used her remaining SkillsFuture Credit to offset a part of the course fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through the course, she learnt about climate issues, sustainable supply chains and green finance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: She is now a Sustainability Client Engagement Specialist at the Singapore Environment Council.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme seeks to enable more mid-career individuals like Ms Low to pursue a substantive bout of upskilling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: If you are a Singaporean aged 40 and above, you will soon be notified by SSG of your eligibility for the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Given the wide range of courses available, you may need some help to make a decision.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Do spend some time to chart your skills journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: There are various ways for you to seek advice: (i) you can refer to online resources, such as MySkillsFuture website and SSG's reports to understand skills that are in demand; (ii) you can also use the CareersFinder tool on the MyCareersFuture portal to discover career opportunities and skills gaps based on your personal profile and work history; and (iii) if you prefer to speak to someone, you can go to a Skills Ambassador for personalised course recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Skills Ambassadors can be found at some community clubs, Workforce Singapore (WSG) Careers Connect Centres, job fairs and SkillsFuture roadshows across the island.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It can involve self-discovery, seeking out advice and more than one bout of skills training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As we shift SkillsFuture to a higher gear, we hope that every individual will take charge of their career health and invest in building their own career resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Jean See and Ms Usha Chandradas highlighted freelancers and self-employed persons as a group that deserves attention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Under the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, there are a good number of courses in the areas highlighted by the Member, whether to deepen technical skills or broaden business skills, such as digital branding and business administration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked how we can ensure that the courses that qualify for the $4,000 top-up are accessible to PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We have been working closely with SG Enable and training providers to make mainstream training programmes more accessible to PwDs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: As there is a wide spectrum of learning needs for PwDs, we also encourage those interested in the courses to approach the training providers who can then work with the Enabling Academy to assess what assistive support and course modifications could be made to suit specific needs of the individual.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We are encouraged that more employers are participating in training, especially the small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: This is a 15% increase from 2022, driven by small companies with fewer than 50 employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: But from the Forward Singapore conversations, we have also heard feedback that opportunities for employer-sponsored training are uneven.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Some workers hope that their employers can do more.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We want to support companies in making training more accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: First, we have developed tools that can help companies assess their skills stock, especially for SMEs that tend to have leaner human resources (HR) departments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Together with JobKred, SSG has developed a tool called the Skills Profiler.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It allows employers to benchmark the skillsets of their employees against similar jobs in the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Companies will then receive customised course recommendations for any skills gaps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I encourage companies to come forward and try this out.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Mark Lee suggested treating workplaces as extensions of our IHLs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Indeed, workplace learning as a modality provides an authentic learning environment for employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It also helps employers better manage the challenges around releasing staff to attend external courses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Last year, we piloted the Workplace Skills Recognition (WPSR) programme in selected Progressive Wage Model (PWM) sectors with the help of the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning (NACE).

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: NACE has started certifying companies that have established workplace learning systems and skills development plans for their staff.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Once certified, the companies will be able to move quickly help their staff into training and to help them acquire WSQ certifications for the skills they have attained at the workplace.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We will expand the WPSR so that more employers and workers can benefit from it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Employers who decide to send their staff for external training can also receive substantive support for training costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In addition to SSG's subsidies, companies can tap on $10,000 of SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit (SFEC) to further defray their out-of-pocket costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: I encourage companies to make full use of these measures to upskill their employees to stay competitive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Our jobs and skills ecosystem must come together to address job transformation and skills needs effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We agree with Members on the need for industry involvement in the design and delivery of training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG, as the national skills authority, works closely with sector agencies and industry partners to understand industry demand and skills needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: These are translated into skills insights that are publicly available so that everyone can make use of the information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: For example, training providers have developed SkillsFuture Series courses to provide skills top-ups in Industry 4.0 and the care, digital and green economies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In areas like AI, where we are making a national push to develop a pipeline of AI talent and AI practitioners, there are a variety of options ranging from bite-sized modular courses to Master’s programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Industry players have stepped in to deliver training as well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: BCG has trained close to 1,000 individuals in business-relevant digital skills through its Rise series of courses for companies and individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Meanwhile, our IHLs are ramping up industry attachments for their staff and tapping on industry practitioners to deliver CET.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har suggested introducing a SkillsFuture quality accreditation framework to differentiate funding for training programmes by quality and industry relevance and recognise high-quality training providers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: SSG has, indeed, moved in this direction with its outcome-based funding model.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: By end-2024, all courses that deliver strong manpower outcomes in terms of securing employment and career progression will be accorded the highest tier of SSG subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To strengthen the reach and impact of SkillsFuture in more challenging sectors, we have introduced new partnership models in the past few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Intermediaries, like the Jobs-Skills Integrators and Queen Bee companies, can help smaller companies leverage on their industry networks and strengths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: To enhance our students' arts and cultural appreciation, MOE regularly reviews our curricular and co-curricular learning opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: An example is the Performing Arts-Based Learning (PABL), which was piloted in 2023 across 22 secondary schools to create authentic learning opportunities beyond the classroom for our lower secondary students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Through PABL, students experience live music performance that is specially produced and staged at a professional concert venue, as well as pre- and post-concert music lessons held in class.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: We received positive feedback from our students and will progressively roll out PABL to all secondary schools from 2024 to 2027.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Last but not least, parents; they are our key partners in supporting students' well-being and development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Dr Wan Rizal, Ms Denise Phua and Assoc Prof Razwana Begum asked how MOE is partnering parents in supporting our students’ holistic development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: MOE has developed resources for parents to guide their children on the various pathways available and in areas, such as children’s well-being, cyber wellness and broadening the definition of "success".

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: If you have the Parents Gateway app on your mobile phone, you will find a treasure trove of parenting resources that can make you a more informed parent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: COMPASS members have led several projects that offer alternative platforms for parents to learn from professionals and other experienced parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: In journeying with parents, our Parent Support Groups (PSGs) have been great partners and I am most thankful to our PSGs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Many volunteer and stay on the PSG even after their children have graduated from the school.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Their passion is to help other parents and be peer supporters for the parent community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Mr Chairman, it takes a whole-of-society effort to equip Singaporeans with the skills they need to adapt and thrive.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: It is our duty to build on the foundation of lifelong learning that has been laid.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
text: Collectively, we can build a brighter shared future for Singaporeans and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, may I take this opportunity to say more about MOE's Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) lesson on the Israel-Hamas conflict, building on what I had said in my interview with the media last week.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This issue has stirred strong emotions amongst many.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is also reflected in the range of PQs filed by Members for upcoming Sittings.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I thought I will say something here today to allow Members more time than the 30 minutes Question Time on Thursday.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The key questions raised were: why conduct such a lesson?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Can MOE teach such a complex and emotive issue effectively?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: What are the learning points from this episode?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Chair, CCE is an established and integral part of the holistic education we provide to our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We teach CCE in schools because we know how important yet how difficult it is to build our national identity amid the larger forces, including civilisational and religious forces that our multiracial, multi-religious society is subject to.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We know how global and social media news and fake news compete every moment to pull our people in different directions, challenging our efforts to maintain national cohesion and harmony.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We do not have the luxury of time or a geographical buffer to insulate our people, including and especially our very young.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We need to equip our people, starting with our young, with the skills and values to navigate this fast pace, often divisive and confusing world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The latest escalation of the Israel-Hamas conflict is a stark reminder that external events can affect our people in different ways and even fracture our society if not well managed.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The young and old can get into heated conversations, insensitive and disrespectful remarks may be made, misinformation abound, especially online.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Different parties appeal to our emotions to side with their cause, and information war is being fought all around us.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We risk being drawn into other people's fights and conflicts.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is why the CCE lessons on contemporary issues often draw from events happening around us to help students better navigate the vagaries of the world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We can neither shelter our children from the world nor keep the world from intruding into their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is also not meant to bring other people's politics into our schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I hope all Singaporeans can agree with us on the intent and importance of CCE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The question then is: what do we do in schools to achieve these shared objectives, especially when dealing with sensitive issues like this?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For the teachers, by now, our teachers have had a few weeks of experience preparing and teaching the package.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have also heard some of their reflections.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some were initially unsure whether they had sufficient content mastery to teach the lesson.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some needed more time to process their own views and feelings about the conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And for those who were still uncomfortable and had asked to be excused from conducting the lesson, their school leaders supported their requests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: By and large, most took on the challenge and carried out their duties professionally because they understood the importance of the task.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are grateful to them for stepping up despite any initial hesitations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To conduct CCE lessons well, our teachers will require facilitation skills, much more than just content mastery, and this is not an easy task.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For students, some schools which have conducted CCE lessons have also shared feedback from their students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: A Primary 6 student said, "We should pray for all the innocent victims of the war and cherish the harmony and peace we have in Singapore." In one secondary school, some students asked their teachers for more information on why the war started in the first place and why the leaders on both sides could not come to a resolution.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of them expressed sadness about the tragic situation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: A first-year junior college student said the CCE lesson was beneficial, as the information presented did not force him to agree on a certain stand on the matter but gave him the space to have his thoughts and considerations towards the issue.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some students also asked thoughtful questions like: "Is there a way out of this circle of violence and hatred?" and "What else can we do to help?" These student voices reflect the intent and learning objectives of the CCE lesson which I described earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have also received much feedback from parents and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some thought the issue was too difficult for Primary 5 and 6 students to understand.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some questioned why some slides seemed to focus only on the more recent events in the long history of the conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Others wondered if the historical context of the conflict was properly emphasised in this CCE lesson.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Yet others felt that we should give our students more information on Singapore's position on the Israel-Palestine issue.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But will this be better for our students and society in the long term?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: If we agree on the intent of CCE, then we must keep striving to improve our delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are fully committed to equipping our teachers to help our children better navigate this complex world.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will also improve our teaching methods based on the experiences gained.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First, we will customise the lesson material further for students of different age groups.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: At this point, let me emphasise that this CCE lesson was not meant to teach the Israel-Palestine history or Middle East politics.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is impossible to do so in an hour-long session, and it was never our intention in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For younger students, we will simplify our material even more.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our focus will continue to be on sensitising our younger ones to the plight of the innocent victims, how they can express sympathy for and empathise with others, and how they can manage their emotions regarding the conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For the older students, we will also teach them to be more discerning of different sources of information.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For the most mature students, we will update the lesson material based on more recent events and help them better understand Singapore's national interests.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan had set out at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' (MFA) COS last week some of these recent developments and how Singapore is responding.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To reiterate, after the 7 October attack, we said Singapore recognised Israel's right to self-defence.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: But Israel's military response has gone too far.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will also explain to our students Singapore's principled position on the Israel-Palestine issue over the decades – and this is for the older students – such as how Singapore had voted in favour of calling for an immediate ceasefire at international platforms, how we have contributed to capacity-building efforts to the Palestinian authority and how we will continue doing our part to advance international efforts towards reaching a two-state solution at the UN.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will certainly continue to reflect the diversity of views from our community within our lesson material and it is a key learning objective for our students to understand how to manage differences and diversity with respect and sensitivity.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: To the extent possible, we will also design the lesson material to avoid parts being taken out of context selectively.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Second, beyond updating the material, we will also better equip our teachers to engage their students in this CCE lesson.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For teachers who would like the extra support, we will organise extra CCE workshops for them to go through the lesson plans with specialists and experienced teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Where appropriate, we will involve resource persons to assist with these workshops.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is in addition to the current suite of teachers' preparations within schools.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Given the diversity of backgrounds and experiences of our teachers, some schools have adopted useful approaches, like organising their teachers in teams to conduct the CCE lesson, which enhances the quality of delivery.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For example, Jurongville Secondary School carried out this lesson with a pair of teachers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: One teacher focused on facilitating the discussion in class while the other looked out for the emotional well-being of students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In Yishun Innova Junior College, the history teacher did a large group briefing on the historical context of the conflict before students discussed the issue further in smaller groups facilitated by their CCE teacher.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For a sensitive topic like the Israel-Hamas conflict, having teachers from different backgrounds and faiths to conduct the lesson together is also a powerful example to our students of how, while we can have different beliefs, we can come together as Singaporeans to discuss complex issues sensitively and respectfully.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are also making broader efforts to train teachers to teach CCE.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: There is a corps of specialised CCE teachers in the teaching fraternity who are available to mentor their colleagues.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Speak with your school leaders who will support you in carrying out your professional duties.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: For us at MOE, there were other useful learning points from this episode.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: First learning point: we cannot underestimate the damage that misrepresentation can cause.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some online commentators selectively picked out one slide out of many in an MOE lesson deck which was circulated last week, asserting that the schools were telling the students the situation in Israel and Gaza only started on 7 October 2023.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In addition, MOE had provided background material on historical developments behind the conflict to help teachers better understand the context.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This was meant to be shared with students who wished for more information on the history rather than for the teacher to teach history to the whole class, which is not the learning objective of this CCE lesson.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This is, indeed, a sobering reminder that in the online space, it is not always easy to separate those who question the material with well-meaning intentions from those who join the fray with ulterior intent to stir up negative emotions on an already sensitive topic.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our second learning point: managing differences respectfully is still a work in progress.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: By and large, Singaporeans express our views in a civil and respectful way.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Still, some of the online vitriol and anger towards MOE and our teachers from this episode remind us that we cannot take this for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some educators have received rude and abusive comments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have come across one picture of an educator being circulated online.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The caption contained a racial slur, insulting her as an uneducated person of her ethnicity and encouraged others to make this educator's photo go viral online.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: While we may disagree on issues, personal attacks and racial slurs against fellow Singaporeans cannot be condoned.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have to be positive role models for our children.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our third learning point: we must be very watchful for potential external interference.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some external online parties have taken an active interest in our discussions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Some show no hesitation to join in the discussions and add their comments to incite anger and unhappiness.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Yet others try to play on Singaporeans' conscience to adopt their positions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It is not difficult to guess the agenda of these external parties.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We have to be careful to not fall prey to their attempts to rile up our people and undermine our cohesion.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Fourth learning point: our unity depends on sustained commitment and effort.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Many of them shared the challenges they encountered and how they had overcome them.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: It has certainly not been an easy time for our teachers and principals.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: In response, many of my principals shared this.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We asked ourselves: how can we allow the seeds of hatred and distrust to be planted in our next generation?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: How can we allow our society to be split by this and other similar issues?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: When we look back in years to come, would we have discharged our duty as educators if our people became more divided, unable to respond as one, view each other with suspicion or become unable to manage differences or diversity respectfully and sensitively?

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I drew comfort and confidence from their conviction.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Indeed, it is our duty to guide the next generation well, help them develop good character and values and build a sound foundation for them to thrive in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: My MOE colleagues and I feel the weight of our mission.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We are determined to discharge our duty and do right by our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I extend my deepest gratitude to all who have given us your feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We will continue to work with you all as partners in education so that we can plant the seeds of hope and harmony in the next generation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This remains a work in progress and we are fully committed to keep on improving.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Our teachers and principals asked if they would have the public support in this important yet challenging task.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I hope Members of this House and the public will do, too.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Let us stand united as Singaporeans to support this important yet challenging effort for the sake of our children and the future of Singapore.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I see a lot of Members wanting to ask clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will try my best to make sure that everyone who has raised their hand will be given an opportunity.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Chairman, I have three clarifications as part of the announcements by the political officeholders at this year's MOE COS.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I think it is good and welcomed news.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I am seeing greater disruption, digitalisation and a lot of new in-demand skills.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I provided feedback that beyond a diploma, can we also support a second university course?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I know we do that for Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs), but can we do that?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Second question is on the entry to polytechnic first year.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: The Minister just announced the consideration of an additional G2 subject for those wanting to enter first year in the polytechnics.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Can the Minister take the suggestion that beyond just one G2, since we are supporting SBB, why not even two G2 subjects?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
