text: Lastly, for the third announcement on the additional $4,000 SkillsFuture Credits for the mature workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Can we consider allowing, beyond those programmes that the Minister has fleshed out programmes, for example, career coaching and counselling, which are crucial?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Because we see a lot of disconnect and dislocation with the mature workers.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: Can we allow that money to be used for not just career transition programmes but also career coaching, specifically, and counselling?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chair, let me address the three questions in turn.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We understand that there are calls for us to extend this to a second degree and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have not precluded extending this to other training programmes, so long as they are good for the people to start a second career or there is a substantive reason for them to take on other roles.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But as to eventually how much we can extend and to what programmes will depend on the quality of the programmes, the relevance of the programmes, as many Members shared, and also depends on our budget space.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, that is the first comment and we note that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the second one, can we allow more than one G2 subject to be considered for polytechnic?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not preclude revising this in the future, based on the experience gained from those who enter polytechnic with one G2 subject first.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the third question, at this point in time, we do not use the SkillsFuture Credit for counselling yet because they can access this through some other means, such as through the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we want to focus the resources on the programme course itself rather than the counselling.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But we will review this and MOM will be making subsequent announcements on how we intend to help people make the right choices on the type of courses that they might want to consider for the next step of their career.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One is directed at the Second Minister on the non-Tamil Indian Languages (NTIL) framework.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think the Second Minister did mention that the last time the grants for NTILs were reviewed was in 2022.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm when the grants were last increased?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the review mean that the grants also went up?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I would appreciate if the Second Minister could confirm that fact.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And if not, when was the last time that was done?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I did not expect Minister to respond to some of the questions that had been filed on the Israel-Hamas issue and the CCE curriculum.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My question in my PQ was about lessons learned.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think Minister has covered quite a few of these lessons quite extensively, so I render my support to the Ministry's work in trying to ensure that the public conversation is a bit more even-handed and even keeled.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I want to assure Mr Singh that when we reviewed it, we looked at the funding required.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And as of now, since the last review until now, we assess that the funding will sufficiently safeguard.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The funding that we give to the Board of Teaching and Testing of the South Asian Languages will not undermine and will safeguard the quality of the teaching and the learning of the NTIL students.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I will have to check and get back to you on that.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I just have one final clarification to make, which is the issue of Personal Learning Devices (PLDs) for primary school students.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I believe I mentioned this in my Budget Debate speech and I mentioned it again in my cut.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I am sorry if I missed a reply, but I was here for most of the responses.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: If Minister or our political officeholders have not answered that, could I please strongly advocate for that and perhaps get MOE's comment on whether this is something that they are committed to doing?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I understand it will take time, but they have done a wonderful job with the secondary school PLDs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, MOE has indeed considered this issue very seriously about whether we should issue PLDs to our primary school students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have also done some pilot studies to see whether it is effective and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The reason is because it is not just about the device.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Also, we need the guidance to make sure that the devices are used appropriately.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we are fully committed to leveraging on technology to the extent possible to enhance the quality of teaching in our classes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But as to the ownership of the device, we will need further studies before we come to a conclusion where we can balance the benefits with the potential downsides of having the youngest students in our cohort managing the devices on their own.

speaker: The Chairman
text: There are many Members wanting to seek clarification.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will give priority to those who have filed cuts.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Members, please keep clarifications short, and from the front bench, likewise, responses short.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I have questions for Minister Maliki and Minister Chan.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: My question is, were there instances where the CCE lesson on the Israel-Hamas war was delivered lecture-style to several classes at the same time?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, would MOE consider ensuring that CCE lessons on sensitive and controversial subjects are conducted in small classes, so there is more opportunity for discussion and dialogue not just between teachers and students, but also between students facilitated by the teacher?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I appreciate the examples shared by Minister about the junior colleges, but can this be standardised across all the schools?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Second, to Minister Maliki, I understand that MOE spends more money per student on SPED schools than in mainstream schools, but I am sure Minister Maliki appreciates that parents of students with special needs often have also higher medical expenses and intervention programme costs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, in the interest of equity and inclusivity, can MOE move towards making all public school fees the same for both SPED and mainstream schools?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I appreciate that in this Budget, it has been lowered to $90.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: But the gulf between $13 and $90 is still quite significant.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, indeed, that is what we are doing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because different schools have different capacities and different needs, so they will organise their sessions based on their capacities and needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Some schools have adopted a two-tier approach whereby the one that is more knowledgeable of the context sets the context and then they allow the discussions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we fully agree with the Member that for many of these, we need smaller discussions because the students are trying to grapple with their own emotions.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, in fact, we have a pedagogy that is called "Think, Pair and Share".

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, the two persons start sharing about their different perspectives and then coming to recognise each other's differences and diversity of perspective, learning to empathise with one another before we go into the bigger group sharing.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We fully understand, fully appreciate and fully empathise with families with children with special education needs.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is really because of the differentiation in the SPED school because the SPED school also varies; not all of them have similar fees.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We try to make sure that, on balance, more of those who are able to bring the fees down, it is more equivalent to our national schools.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But we will work with the SPED schools, because in the SPED schools they also have got different variations in terms of their disabilities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And some schools with higher disability needs that they are responding to do have higher fees.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We will work with those schools to see how we can help them.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For our students in those schools that really do need further help, we have worked with the SPED schools and encouraged them to go to the SPED schools and get further assistance.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And where possible, we will continue to support these schools and these students.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Chair, I have two clarifications for Minister Maliki.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: If I understood the Minister correctly, there will be sufficient opportunities to integrate students with disabilities in mainstream schools.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister share some examples highlighting how this can be achieved?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: My second question is, will MOE consider proactively including students with disabilities into activities, like physical education lessons?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And when they are in the mainstream school, they go through a similar programme as the other students, including physical education, where abilities are commensurate to their disabilities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We are also working towards creating opportunities for mainstream schools to partner SPED schools so that they can continue to also provide opportunities for students from mainstream school, whether they do have peers who are special needs in their schools or not, so that they can continue to also appreciate interactions with students from SPED schools.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: I understand that SSG relies on job transformation maps and industry transformation maps (ITMs) to determine the courses to fund.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: However, these maps address companies' employment needs, then the needs of freelancers who are actually engaged by businesses to augment their operational needs in specialised areas.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Freelancers, like coaches and creators, want to partake in all these different initiatives because staying relevant is actually more urgent and pressing for them.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: And therefore, they ask for relevant training that is applicable to their work and must be valued by the service buyers, who also include Government agencies.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
text: Could the Minister of State share what approach would SSG take in its approach to course curation, to cater to the needs of freelancers?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Chan, Minister Maliki and Minister of State Gan for sharing MOE's plans.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I also appreciate Minister Chan's clarification and the way forward to improve our CCE curriculum.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: At the top of my head, I am always thinking about the teachers, and I do believe that they need to be protected, especially when certain things are happening online in terms of abuse and online harm.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: What are the plans for us to protect them?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I remember we had the issue in the Ministry of Health (MOH) last year and we did well to issue a Protection from Online Manipulation Act (POFMA) direction to all these false stories online.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Given the evolving nature of global events and the way in which unverified slides and materials, purportedly from the CCE, are being circulated online, how does MOE incorporate the feedback from the various stakeholders, including parents, educators and students, in the development and review of the CCE curriculum?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I wonder if the PSGs can play a bigger role in trying to address these issues?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: At the top of my head, I also wonder if we can issue a POFMA direction to such platforms for circulating certain slides.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, first, let me thank both sides of the House for their support for our educators and their support for them in conducting this very challenging CCE lesson.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I have studied very closely the last few years why countries do well and do not do well for their Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) and their educational outcomes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And even in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) report, it comes out very clearly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I asked myself this very difficult question: what determines the quality of the teachers?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Is it because of the pay that we give them?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When a society loses the respect for their teachers, when their teachers feel disrespected and hassled, no good people want to join the teaching service, then, regardless of the policies, regardless of the infrastructure and the investment that we have, it will come to naught.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We have come to this one conclusion that even the slides will not do justice to the teaching done by the teachers because the slides do not speak.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For parents or the public who have concerns about this, we would rather meet them face-to-face and explain to them how the slides are used.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because we have tested this and no matter how we try to make the slides public or available, if it is done selectively without interpretation, we will still come back to the same issue.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Every teacher must know their own students to customise their teaching accordingly.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But, yet, at the same time, we must protect our teachers to not have them be subjected to the pressures from all different sources to change the material according to their versions of the event.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we find a balance between these two.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I will encourage interested parties to contact us and let us go through with you how a lesson is conducted beyond just what is said in the slides.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My clarification relates to the Minister's response on my call for a through-train pilot programme.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister said that if we see our worth as being defined by examination results, only removing the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) will not remove the stress and neither is removing all stress our goal.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Instead, we need to help our students manage and overcome stress.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Whatever we may say, action speaks louder than words and what parents see are the effects of PSLE results on their children's educational path.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Instead, on the other hand, making PSLE optional will send the message that primary education is not just about the PSLE score and removing the PSLE will not remove all the stress.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the Minister not agree that children will have stresses in their lives beyond PSLE?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There will be annual school examinations, stresses in other areas of their lives, like relationships with parents, siblings, classmates and friends.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister also made the point on how we select students who are suitable for through-train at the age of six and if we cannot select, how do we support the diverse learning profile, and that PSLE and SEC are a means to help students find a suitable learning environment.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I wish to clarify that the point here is not for MOE to select, but to give parents the choice.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Those who believe that all the time, energy and resources put in to prepare students for the PSLE and dealing with all the stresses can be put to better use elsewhere to teach them real-life skills and encourage their natural curiosity towards the unknown.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Hazel Poa, I have given you a lot of latitude.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Does the Minister agree that the annual school examinations and regular assessments can already serve the purpose of identifying different learning needs of students, and SBB within the school can assist in differentiated learning without overtaxing our teachers?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, I understand that Ms Hazel Poa was not in the Chamber when I gave my answer last Friday.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Maybe Ms Hazel Poa would like to go through what I have said and consider it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: As I have said, every idea is not without merits.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not about not giving choices to the parents.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is about how we support our students for the next 10 years, given their diverse abilities, given their diverse needs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Can we do all of these in one school?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Ultimately, exams are but a means for us to help our students find the most appropriate environment to learn for the next stage.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is always to surpass ourselves more than to surpass others.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I think it is important that we provide an opportunity for our students to discuss current affairs in CCE, as they are already presented with this information.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: But one challenge of doing this is emotions can, indeed, be very raw and it requires masterful facilitation in order to achieve the intended objective.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: So, a few supplementary questions for our Minister.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I welcome the suggestion that we should do it in pairs or at least provide some guidance to the teachers or some support to the teachers while they go through it for the first few trials.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Second, I welcome the Minister's reply that the information is to be updated.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can I suggest that we share the instances where we re-voted for ceasefire and support for humanitarian assistance, suggested in October 2023, in February, and in the past 50 years, on our stand on supporting humanitarian rights?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: And before we restart it again, can we trial the lessons with a focus group or with a pilot group of individuals and get their feedback on it?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: On information, in particular, there are rumours that the infamous Samuel and Arun slide was not created by MOE.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can the Minister share a bit more insights on to that?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: And lastly, I have raised a PQ on what support is provided to teachers when they receive backlash from parents and the general public, and whether the school management will take action against the teachers who are subjected to these complaints.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I think we need to support our teachers and educators a bit more in this space.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Chair, let me respond to the five points.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First point, indeed, I shared this with my principals personally, when we had our large group sharing in January.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I said when we conduct this lesson, it is not to assign teachers just based on appointment.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, we need teachers who are able and willing, and are able to do this professionally.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why, before they conducted the lessons, the principals and the school leaders had their own internal sessions with the teachers so that they can gauge who is able to do what and then, they can form the composite teams to do this effectively.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Of course, as they do more, they will gather experience.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, one of the principals, during the large group sharing told us this, "We are so inexperienced in this aspect and we need to build our experience to facilitate sensitive conversations respectfully.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We need to do this, but if we do not start, we will never be there." So, indeed, we want to make sure that the teachers do not impose their views and we do this as a session ourselves before we even do it with the students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But for the older students who require these materials, these will be made available to them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is not possible for us to stop everything, because things are evolving.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And even if we do not conduct the lesson, the questions, as the Member said, are being asked by our students and our teachers must know how to respond, how to guide them to respond sensitively and respectfully.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And as I have said in my statement just now, they have MOE's full support and we will also make sure that they have the full support of the law.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I truly, truly appreciate the support of Members of this House, because without your support, others might be emboldened to think that they can take advantage of our teachers, even if they do not agree with what we say, because the respect for our teachers is most important.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They could have decided not to do this and we are no better off as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But the fact that they stepped forward, they do this for us, do this with us, let us do it with them, let us support them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: A last point on the Samuel and Arun slide, there was this slide circulating in the deck that says that MOE trivialised the issue because we equated it with a football match.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: For those of you who are very good at detecting scams, you will know that the background of the slide is also different from the rest of the deck.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But upon investigation, we found out that this particular slide was inserted in one particular school because there is a particular context for the teacher to take the initiative to help their students of this age group to relate to something that is more relatable to them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I do not fault the teachers for that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But what is happening online is that this is then taken out of context to say that this is the MOE slide for everyone, including the junior college students.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is why I say we need to have confidence and trust in our teachers.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our teachers know their students, and they must be able to have some ability to communicate things with their students in the way that is best for them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I really appreciate the Member raising this issue because it is never MOE's intention to trivialise anything.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We do not need to add more complications to the issue.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will squeeze in one or two more clarifications.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I believe this is done similarly for the Ministry's sexuality education.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sexuality education deals with very personal issues and families' beliefs, and so forth.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is talking about if there are diversity of views, there are differences in view, and how we can manage to proceed as one.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is about interpersonal relations, about how we respond as fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The conflict itself is a context, but it is not the key part of it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The conflict, just like any other conflicts, may pull our people in different directions because of their different backgrounds and different beliefs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But the central part of the CCE is to go back to the four things that we mentioned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How do we discuss things respectfully, given and notwithstanding our differences?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How do we build a cohesive society amidst all these challenges?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I go back to what I said.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our identity is being formed, and it is never easy because we can always be seen as part of some other larger civilisation forces.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And our challenge is not to discard our past and build a new future without a past.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have reached the end of the clarification phase.

speaker: The Chairman
text: In fact, we have gone over 30 minutes and the guillotine time has been reached.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, can I invite Mr Patrick Tay to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: I want to place on record our thanks to the MOE staff, SSG staff, as well as all the educators and trainers across Singapore for banding together and making a difference to all of us and to ensure we stay ready, relevant and resilient – ready with new skills and knowledge, relevant to the new jobs and the future and resilient to the new changes and many curveballs that are hurled at us.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
